category_title: Overage 8th-grade students at risk of dropping out
scenario_title: Designing and revising sensitive survey questions
minimal_context: The student is revising a survey on a laptop to print and distribute to fellow students to gather information for a documentary.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's review the survey you are revising on the laptop to print out and distribute to your fellow students.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Moving desks closer together) I feel a lot of people will answer ‘yes’ to this one. You know why? Cause I have a LOT of friends like that.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: How are you planning to handle the completed surveys?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: We want to make sure students feel safe returning their surveys. We decided it would be better to put them in a shoe-box, put tape around it, and then decorate it to ensure security.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You need to rewrite some of these items. Questions like the ones about abortion are too probing and should be knocked off the survey.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: No, you’re going too fast! You have to slow down, man. Don’t rush it. Sex questions you always leave for the end. You sugar-coat them at first. And then you crack them!

task.content: revising a survey they plan to print out and distribute to their fellow students
task.learning_goal: gather accurate information, and then create and disseminate new knowledge to the public.

context.materials: laptop, large poster paper with marker in hand
context.social_setting: desks closer together... next to and facing each other
context.time_context: after school until 6pm twice a week

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: supervising teacher urged them to rewrite it, since she said it was 'too probing.' (Other questions she said should be 'knocked off' the survey such as whether students had ever had an abortion.)
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: heated discussion about how to make sure students felt safe in returning their surveys... Some discussion ensued as to whether oral sex was actually sex.
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: thinking as researchers as they seek to gather accurate information
related_quotes: No, you’re going too fast! You have to slow down, man. Don’t rush it. Sex questions you always leave for the end. You sugar-coat them at first. And then you crack them!
I feel a lot of people will answer ‘yes’ to this one. You know why? Cause I have a LOT of friends like that.

behavior_patterns.condition: When one student suggested they keep the filled-in surveys in a shoe-box
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: others were against the idea since they said it could be opened. The first student then decided it would be better to put tape around it and then decorate it
behavior_patterns.internal_state: make sure students felt safe in returning their surveys
